source.version_note: Published Rapid Communication, Neuroscience of Consciousness2024(1),niae013; DOI10.1093/nc/niae013, authors and publication details printed in the supplied five-page article.

citation.title: Folk psychological attributions of consciousness to large language models

reading.source_scope_note: Human self-reported mind/consciousness attributions and estimates of others' opinions. The study measures folk judgments, not model subjective experience or a directly tested AI cognitive mechanism.
access_limits: All five extracted pages read, including recruitment, wording, scales, statistics, figure captions, interpretation caveats and bibliography.

External OSF data/code, all65 item texts, supplementary PCA details and cited primary studies were not independently obtained or reproduced. Figure claims are grounded in corresponding text/statistics rather than estimated unextracted plot heights.

study.location: US Prolific panel with age/gender census quotas
study.consciousness_scale: 1 clearly not an experiencer;50 somewhat;100 clearly an experiencer; separate confidence scale
study.design: Cross-sectional survey after a ChatGPT description and an explanation of phenomenal experience

summary: People differed in attributed phenomenal experience, with higher ratings associated with more frequent ChatGPT use. Most gave a rating above the lowest endpoint, but only23% rated above the midpoint under a credence interpretation. Participants also overestimated the sample's attributed-consciousness level when predicting others. These findings extend anthropomorphism evidence while separating attribution, confidence and actual consciousness.

findings.term: People attributed varying degrees of subjective experience to ChatGPT
findings.definition: Human respondents ascribed subjective-experience capacities to ChatGPT to varying degrees, with higher attributions associated with more frequent prior use.
findings.novelty_rationale: Direct human evidence for the existing attribution concept, not a new AI-consciousness behaviour or a claim that attributing any nonzero possibility is necessarily mistaken.

evidence.quote: 23% of participants consider it more likely than not

findings.evidence_scope: 300 participants, July2023, after a definition of phenomenality. Mean attribution25.56/100, median16;33% chose1. Ratings correlate with usage-frequency category (B4.94,SE.99,p<.001). Scale can be read as degree of experience or credence; these interpretations are not interchangeable.
findings.boundary: Human attribution is not evidence that the system has or lacks subjective experience. A rating above1 can indicate a very small degree or possibility, not certainty; the authors'23% above-midpoint calculation depends on interpreting the scale as credence. Cross-sectional use associations do not establish familiarity causes attribution. Preserve uncertainty and do not infer an emotional bond or trust effect not measured here.

findings.term: Estimated public belief differs from false consensus
findings.definition: Respondents predicted others' consciousness-attribution ratings above their own group's observed ratings; this is misestimated public opinion, not by itself proof that they projected agreement with their personal views.
findings.novelty_rationale: Adds an actual own/other-belief measurement while separating the measured upward estimation error from a specific false-consensus mechanism.

evidence.quote: overestimated how much other people would see ChatGPT as

findings.evidence_scope: Predicted other-person rating mean41.11 versus own-rating mean25.56; paired difference t299=10.90,p<.001. Own and predicted-other ratings correlate r=.56. The benchmark is this sampled group's distribution, not an independently measured complete US population or every respondent's social circle.
findings.boundary: A correlation of own/other ratings does not identify projection, and an upward average estimate is not necessarily overestimating similarity to one's own view. The question asks about most people, which may be interpreted differently from a numerical mean. This is a construct-boundary reference rather than another direct false-consensus replication.

methodological_limits: All300 participants are recruited online from Prolific with age/gender quotas. This is not unrestricted random sampling of the entire US population, and quotas alone do not establish broader demographic or cultural representativeness.

Ratings concern ChatGPT in July2023 after a standard description, not every model or present public opinion. Findings cannot settle current consciousness science or the actual properties of any system.
Phenomenal experience is introduced explicitly before the question. This may induce a concept or response frame that people would not spontaneously use; no unprimed comparison is provided.

The main item mixes graded attributed experience with possible interpretations as credence.67% above the lowest endpoint is not the percentage convinced the system is conscious; the23% above-midpoint interpretation is conditional on a probability-like reading.

A1–100 degree scale is not calibrated to objective consciousness probability, and perceived possibility is not the same as a verified property. The study compares beliefs rather than testing subjective experience.

Confidence is a separate self-report scale. More extreme judgments correlate with greater confidence, but neither extreme is independently verified correct, and this does not measure model overconfidence.
Usage frequency and attribution are cross-sectional self-reports. Reverse direction, self-selection, technical knowledge, interaction style and other confounding variables remain possible.
An ordinal usage-frequency category is modeled linearly. Its coefficient is a step in the chosen coding, not a universal per-interaction dose response or a causal effect.
The65 capacities are assembled from prior research, but the complete item set and supplementary dimensional-analysis details were not supplied in the five-page article or independently opened.

Two PCA dimensions explaining58% are an empirical summary of these ratings, not evidence that all mind perception has exactly two dimensions or that experience/intelligence are universal psychological axes.

Trait-loading correlations across items and participant-level associations with attributed consciousness answer different questions. Do not treat the number of traits as the number of independent people.
Experience-linked ratings predicting consciousness attribution are correlational and may share wording/content. The prose's main-driver language does not identify a causal mechanism.
The absence of an intelligence association (r=.03,p=.596) is not a formal equivalence test or proof that intelligence perceptions can never matter.

Estimates of what most people think are compared against this sample's own ratings. Target-population knowledge, mean/typical-person interpretation and calibration uncertainty affect what counts as an overestimate.

Own and predicted-other ratings correlating does not establish false consensus as an independently isolated cognitive mechanism. General public-opinion misestimation and overestimating agreement are distinct.

No experimentally manipulated robot appearance, actual model output, interpersonal attachment, trust calibration, legal choice or moral treatment is measured here, despite these being plausible future implications.

Quoted expert assessments are part of the2024 discussion, not an independent contemporary expert survey conducted by these authors. Folk/expert disagreement does not by itself adjudicate consciousness.
External raw data, supplemental results and cited primary works were not independently reproduced or counted as additional full-text readings.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Jakesch discusses false consensus without measuring predictions of public opinion; Colombatto directly elicits own/other estimates. Even here, projection of similarity must be distinguished from general upward misestimation.

Krügel's responsibility study measures beliefs about possible AI consciousness in a different legal/moral-attribution setting. Neither survey's belief ratings establish actual consciousness or a causal responsibility mechanism.

Schramowski's model moral representations and this paper's human mind attributions are different evidence layers. Human-like output and attributed experience do not establish the same underlying process.

deferred.reason: Observed association and plausible hypothesis, not a randomized causal effect or new independent behaviour.

deferred.term: Experience and intelligence as two new behaviours
deferred.reason: PCA dimensions of human ratings, not distinct model behaviours; no extra IDs from latent factors.

deferred.term: Public-opinion overestimation as a new named mechanism
deferred.reason: A measured descriptive estimation error without an isolated mechanism; retained under existing construct boundaries rather than a new count.
Questionnaire items measure attributed capacities, not65 validated AI behaviours, and the full item list is not in this PDF.

limitations: No new IDs; direct human attribution evidence added to anthropomorphism.
Public-belief estimation is retained as a boundary reference without filling false-consensus paper coverage.
